_comment: Destination-level text for /hvac-technician/ohio. originShared applies to every origin row; merged from the records' own wording with the origin made generic. Quotation marks only around text verbatim in the named registered source.

originShared.text: OCILB publishes reciprocity applications that list HVAC for Alabama, Kentucky, Louisiana, Mississippi, South Carolina, Tennessee, and West Virginia.
OCILB issues state licenses to HVAC contractors who perform commercial work, and the license must be assigned to a "contracting company".

To qualify for the Ohio examination with an out-of-state trades contractors license substantially similar to the Ohio license, provide: proof of the license for at least 5 years (for example, a letter of good standing); proof of at least five authorizations for construction issued by the building authority where you hold the license; at least one tax return showing income earned under the license (plus one W2 if you are not an owner); and proof that your contracting company is licensed as a foreign corporation or registered as a foreign limited liability company with a designated agent in Ohio.
The application does not say how OCILB decides whether a license is substantially similar.
